pages.summary: Graphs: nodes joined by edges, undirected or directed, the edges with weights or without.
body: A graph is made from end nodes s and t (numbers or names, an edge from each s(k) to t(k)), with weights, or from an adjacency matrix (A(i, j) nonzero an edge, its value the weight). `graph` makes an undirected one (an edge joins two nodes both ways), `digraph` a directed one (an edge goes from s to t). G.Edges is a table of EndNodes and Weight, kept sorted; G.Nodes a table of the nodes' Name and anything else added. `plot` draws a graph, a digraph's edges with arrowheads.

pages.summary: A graph's size, and its nodes and edges found by name or by their ends.
body: `numnodes` and `numedges` count; `findnode` gives the numbers of nodes named (0 for a name not there); `findedge` the number of the edge joining two nodes (0 where none does), or the end nodes of edges given by number. `edgecount` counts the edges between two nodes, and `ismultigraph` asks whether any pair is joined more than once.
syntax: How many join s and t.

examples.title: Finding things
examples.code:
D = digraph({'a', 'b', 'b', 'c'}, {'b', 'c', 'd', 'd'});
[numnodes(D), numedges(D)]
findnode(D, {'c', 'x'})
findedge(D, 'b', 'd')
[s, t] = findedge(D, 3)
G = graph([1 1 2], [2 3 3]);
edgecount(G, 2, 1)
ismultigraph(addedge(G, 1, 2))

pages.summary: The edges at each node, and the nodes and edges next to a node.
body: `degree` counts the edges meeting each node (a self-loop twice; for a digraph, in and out together), `indegree` and `outdegree` those coming into and leaving a node of a digraph. `neighbors` gives the nodes joined to a node either way, `successors` those a digraph's node points to and `predecessors` those pointing to it. `outedges` and `inedges` give the edges themselves, with the nodes at their other ends.
syntax: The edges out, and their ends.

examples.title: A small directed network
examples.code:
D = digraph([1 1 2 3 4 4], [2 3 3 4 1 2]);
[indegree(D), outdegree(D), degree(D)]
successors(D, 4)'
predecessors(D, 3)'
neighbors(D, 1)'
[eid, nid] = outedges(D, 4)

pages.summary: A graph as a sparse matrix: who is joined to whom, and which edge meets which node.
body: `adjacency` gives A(i, j) = 1 where an edge joins i to j (both ways for a graph), or the weights there with `'weighted'`. `incidence` gives a row for each node and a column for each edge: -1 at an edge's source, 1 at its target. For a graph, I*I' is the Laplacian, the degrees on the diagonal.

examples.title: A weighted triangle with a tail
examples.code:
G = graph([1 1 2 3], [2 3 3 4], [5 2 7 1]);
full(adjacency(G))
full(adjacency(G, 'weighted'))
I = full(incidence(G))
isequal(I*I', full(laplacian(G)))

pages.summary: New graphs from a graph: edges and nodes added or taken away, a part, renumbered, or turned round.
body: A graph is a value: each of these gives a new graph and leaves the one given as it was. `addedge` adds edges (and nodes named or numbered past the last), `rmedge` takes edges away, `addnode` adds nodes joined to nothing, `rmnode` takes nodes away with their edges (the nodes after them numbered down). `subgraph` keeps some nodes and the edges among them, `reordernodes` numbers the nodes in another order, and `flipedge` turns a digraph's edges round.

pages.summary: Shortest paths: between two nodes, between every pair, the nodes within a distance, and the tree of paths from a node.
body: A path's length is the sum of its edges' weights (the number of its edges when there are none, or with `'Method', 'unweighted'`). `shortestpath` gives the nodes along one shortest path, its length and its edges; `distances` the lengths between every pair (Inf where there is no path); `nearest` the nodes within a distance of a node, nearest first; `shortestpathtree` the digraph of the shortest paths from a node to every other. Negative weights need a digraph without a negative cycle (`'Method', 'mixed'`).

examples.title: Roads between five towns

pages.summary: Walking a graph: breadth first, depth first, and every path between two nodes.
body: `bfsearch` visits the nodes in order of their distance in edges from the start, `dfsearch` goes as deep as it can along each branch before coming back; neighbours are taken in the order of their numbers, and `'Restart', true` goes on from the first node not reached until every node has been visited. `allpaths` lists every path between two nodes that visits no node twice, as node lists (and edge lists).

examples.title: A small tree with a shortcut

pages.summary: The parts of a graph: connected components, the parts no single node splits, and a digraph's components as nodes.
body: `conncomp` gives each node's component, components numbered in the order of their first nodes (a digraph's are strongly connected, each node reaching each other, unless `'Type', 'weak'`). `biconncomp` gives each edge's biconnected component and the cut vertices, whose removal splits the graph. `condensation` makes a digraph of the strongly connected components, which has no cycle.
syntax: Each edge's, and the cut vertices.

pages.summary: Order and reach in a digraph: an order every edge goes forward in, cycles, and the edges of reach.
body: `toposort` puts the nodes of a digraph without cycles in an order in which every edge goes forward (of the nodes free to come next, the smallest), and `isdag` asks whether there is no cycle; `hascycles` asks the same of any graph. `transclosure` adds an edge from each node to every node it reaches; `transreduction` keeps the fewest edges that reach as the digraph does.

pages.summary: A minimum spanning tree, and the largest flow through a network.
body: `minspantree` joins the nodes a root reaches with edges of least total weight (`'Type', 'forest'` makes a tree in each component); pred gives each node's parent. `maxflow` treats weights as capacities and gives the largest flow from s to t, the flow on each edge as a digraph, and a minimum cut: the nodes on s's side and on t's, whose edges between carry exactly the maximum flow.
syntax: [mf, GF, cs, ct] = maxflow(G, s, t)

pages.summary: How central each node is, and whether two graphs are the same but for numbering.
body: `centrality` scores nodes: `'degree'` by their edges, `'closeness'` by how near they are to all others, `'betweenness'` by how many shortest paths pass through them, `'pagerank'` and `'eigenvector'` by the importance of their neighbours (these sum to 1); a digraph also has in and out kinds and `'hubs'` and `'authorities'`. `isisomorphic` asks whether the nodes of one graph can be renumbered to give the other.
syntax: Edge lengths for closeness and betweenness.

examples.title: A star and a chain
examples.code:
G = graph([1 1 1 1 5], [2 3 4 5 6]);
centrality(G, 'degree')'
centrality(G, 'betweenness')'
round(centrality(G, 'closeness')', 4)
round(centrality(G, 'pagerank')', 4)
isisomorphic(G, graph([6 6 6 6 2], [1 3 4 2 5]))
isisomorphic(G, graph([1 2 3 4 5], [2 3 4 5 6]))

pages.summary: A graph plot changed: nodes and edges drawn apart, labels, and the nodes placed again.
body: `highlight` draws nodes, edges or a whole subgraph (a path tree, a spanning tree) of a plot apart, in red and larger unless told otherwise; nodes given with `'EdgeColor'` or `'LineWidth'` mark the edges between them too, so a path draws as a path. `labelnode` and `labeledge` label nodes and edges. `layout` places the nodes again: `'force'`, `'layered'` (for a digraph without cycles), `'circle'` or `'subspace'`.
